correctness.rationale: Exact unitary phase conjugation yields real Gram off-diagonals g(d), and explicit eigenvalues handle balanced gaps. Gershgorin/interlacing strictly excludes a gap below q; the only remaining (q,q,q+2) type is excluded by a fully factored eighth-degree inequality positive for every N>=11; N=3,4,5,6,8 handled exactly. All quantifiers, eigenvalue ratios, and optimizer counts checked. The standalone checker independently reproduces three symbolic identities and exhaustively evaluates all frequency triples through N=70; finite tests are corroboration only.

originality.rationale: Specific constrained infinite-family sharp ratio and optimizer-count theorem was compared to published finite-group quantitative-spectrality framework, classical perfect Vandermonde conditioning, and separated/clustered-node estimates; these neither state nor imply it. A qualitative spectral-pair result covers only the 3|N orthogonal subcase; the new nonorthogonal regimes and uniqueness remain distinct. Historical alternative terminology leaves residual risk.
residual_risks: An equivalent older three-by-three restricted Vandermonde minimax theorem may exist under spectral design or interpolation terminology.

value.rationale: Best Riesz ratio measures stability of exponential bases in finite harmonic analysis. The theorem gives exact all-order sharp values, arithmetic dependence on N mod 3, and counts/equality classification of optimal three-grid-frequency designs for the natural three-consecutive-point aperture. This answers a nontrivial discrete minimax problem, not a substitution into generic bounds; the precise optimal design has direct use in stable reconstruction.
